title: Right triangle on the coordinate plane
observableEvidence: Finds the area of a right triangle on the coordinate plane from vertex coordinates in more than one quadrant, using its horizontal and vertical sides, and labels it in square units.
prompt: A triangle has vertices P(-3, -2), Q(5, -2) and R(-3, 4). What is the area of triangle PQR? Include the unit in your answer.
solutionRepresentation: PQ is horizontal: from x = -3 to x = 5 is 8 units. PR is vertical: from y = -2 to y = 4 is 6 units. They meet at a right angle at P. Area = 1/2 × 8 × 6 = 24 square units.
solutionMethod: Find the horizontal and vertical sides from shared coordinates, use them as base and height, take half of their product, and label the area in square units.

deterministicValidator.equivalenceNotes: Whole-answer match after case, spacing and trailing-punctuation normalization; no substring parts. The square unit is required: a bare number, or the number with a linear or missing unit, is not accepted.

hintSteps.prompt: Look for two sides that are horizontal or vertical. They meet at a right angle and can be the base and the height.
hintSteps.question: Which two vertices share a y-coordinate, and which two share an x-coordinate?

hintSteps.prompt: A side that crosses an axis is as long as the distances on both sides of that axis added together.
hintSteps.question: How long are the horizontal side and the vertical side?

hintSteps.prompt: A different triangle with vertices (-1, 1), (3, 1) and (-1, -4) has legs of 4 and 5 units, so its area is 1/2 × 4 × 5 = 10 square units.
hintSteps.question: Using the same steps, what is the area of triangle PQR, with its unit?

accessibilityNotes: Text-only item: all three vertices are given as signed coordinates in the prompt, so no plotted graph or color is needed. The answer is typed with its unit.
accessibleAlternative: Read aloud or display: A triangle has vertices P at negative 3, negative 2; Q at 5, negative 2; and R at negative 3, 4. Find the area of the triangle and write the unit.
